rows.evidence: The only production sourceAuthority is createSourceAuthorityReader({authority: reads.authority, records: backend.records}) at src/composition/create-platform.ts:1022, passed to the one createWorkflow call at :1796. Its load (src/core/work-graph/source-authority-reader.ts:152-161) takes a Run ref into loadSupported, which catches a thrown authority read at :103-106 and wraps the found-ref recheck in a try at :110-116; the QueryJob branch catches readMany at :133-136, and copyExactRef only checks a string map (:65-80). reviewGate reads active.runRef, a Run ref, so no rejection path remains for this caller and the null arm cannot arise.
rows.proposal_note: Deleting the .catch(() => null) and the runRead !== null conjunct is behaviour-neutral; keep the found/status/snapshot checks as the reviewers say. No spec line reserves a rejection path on this port.

rows.evidence: maintenanceArchive is used only as the archive dependency of createSessionMaintenanceService (src/business/workflow/workflow.ts:2843-2855). Maintenance never calls archive.archiveLine: it reads archiveLineInternal through internalArchive() (src/business/workflow/session-maintenance.ts:174-176, called at :682) and continueArchiveLine (:585). createSessionArchiveService always returns archiveLineInternal (src/business/workflow/session-archive.ts:868-874), so the wrapper archiveLine and its inner fallback are never executed, and no other consumer of maintenanceArchive exists.

rows.evidence: The fallback arrow runs only when deps.now is undefined (src/business/workflow/workflow.ts:2921-2925). The only production createWorkflow call passes now (src/composition/create-platform.ts:1812-1814, :1887), itself defaulted at :605, so the arrow is unreachable in production. It is intentional, though: WorkflowDependencies.now is optional and src/business/workflow/ports.ts:125-127 (decision L-g, S:597) says the new Date().toISOString() fallback stays when the clock is not injected.
rows.proposal_note: Do not make now required or delete the fallback: S:597 and ports.ts:125-127 reserve it for non-injected (old narrow) callers, and slice-1 evidence s1-p2g.md:101-105 states the same. The D2 reading is right for production, but the agreed deletion is a spec change; keep the fallback untested.

rows.evidence: writeInput cannot reject: stdin.write is inside try/catch (src/core/workspace/analysis-runner.ts:137), the awaited drain promise only resolves (:139-151), and stdin.end is inside try/catch (:159); stdin.on/once and AbortSignal listener registration do not throw. Its two production callers build header/config/files from JSON strings, string arrays and nulls (src/core/workspace/architecture-language-provider.ts:248-259, :301-311; files capped at 2 MiB at :103), so JSON.stringify cannot throw either. The .catch(() => {}) at :340 therefore never runs.
rows.proposal_note: Deleting the outer catch is safe; keeping it as a crash guard for a future writeInput edit is harmless and no test is owed either way.

rows.evidence: task is the async IIFE at src/core/workspace/capture.ts:582-588: every throw from run(signal) is caught and converted to rejected(...). rejected() and message() cannot throw for the Error values production code throws, and the finally callback only does this.inFlight.delete(task). So neither task nor task.finally(...) can reject, and the .catch(() => {}) at :590 is unreachable.
rows.proposal_note: Deleting the catch is behaviour-neutral; keeping it as a future crash guard is harmless and needs no test.

rows.evidence: U is wrong in the other direction. readStoredDecoded calls decode only after readStoredRecord's readMany returns a record (src/core/work-graph/communication/decision-source-facts.ts:246-253). Both production backends validate every returned record with the registered schema before returning it (src/core/record-store/in-memory-record-store.ts:227-255, src/core/record-store/sqlite-record-store.ts:353-386, applyRecordSchema calls schema.validate), and each owner decoder's first step is that same validate: src/core/work-graph/persistence/record-codecs.ts:743 (Goal), plan-record-codecs.ts:999, completion-record-codecs.ts:205, queries/query-record-codecs.ts:461/564/674, sessions/message-record-codecs.ts:1200. A record that passes the store therefore cannot fail the decoder, so not even a hand-edited or foreign row reaches this damaged callback through the platform's ports; D2, not U.
rows.proposal_note: The reviewers' proposal to keep the diagnostic and add no tamper test is still right (AGENTS.md rule 4), but the reason is the store codec guarantee, not tampering. Do not add a test that bypasses the store's schema; keeping the one-line unavailable mapping is harmless.

rows.evidence: Same guarantee as C4-025 for the saved-answer templates. The callers decode SessionMessage/QueryJobAnswer/QueryRun (src/core/work-graph/communication/decision-source-facts.ts:999-1000, :1024-1025, :1029-1030); the store already applied the same validate these decoders start with (src/core/record-store/in-memory-record-store.ts:249-252; sessions/message-record-codecs.ts:1112-1121 and :1200; queries/query-record-codecs.ts:698-701, :564, :674). readStoredDecoded reaches the damaged callback only if a record returned by readMany fails its own registered validate, which cannot happen. D2, not U.
rows.proposal_note: Keep the required damaged field of ReadRecordTemplates (it is the only decode-failure mapping and deleting it restructures the shared read for no behaviour change), and add no tamper test; classify the arm by the codec guarantee instead of a hand-edited store.

rows.evidence: unavailableFacts is reached only for a moduleFactsOf result that is neither ready, rejected nor not_found (src/core/work-graph/notes/note-anchors.ts:699, :706). Neither producer can return not_ready: the write/dispose seam is note-service.ts:1054-1055 -> catalogModuleFactsOf(readCurrentCatalogWindow(...)); CurrentCatalogWindow is ready|not_found|Rejection (src/core/work-graph/architecture/catalog-service.ts:354-358) and mapStoreFailure turns every StoreFailure into a CoreRejection (:85-97), while catalogModuleFactsOf returns ready/not_found/Rejection (:813-817). The read-model's own anchorFacts leaves catalogModuleFacts unset (note-read-model.ts:344) and uses the fallback readCatalogModuleFacts at :535, but the fallback calls those same two functions (:797-805), so it also cannot return not_ready. D2 stands.
rows.proposal_note: The narrowing as written is incomplete: note-anchors.ts:56 is narrowed, but the fallback readCatalogModuleFacts is still declared ReadResult<CatalogModuleFacts> (catalog-service.ts:797) and is live on the read-model path (note-read-model.ts:535), so after deleting the two facts.status !== 'ready' guards a not_ready from the fallback would be silently returned as ready. Narrow catalogModuleFactsOf/readCatalogModuleFacts too, or keep the guard, which is also what slice-4-SPEC.md:730 requires for a failed catalog read.

rows.evidence: The fallback at src/core/work-graph/notes/note-read-model.ts:436-440 is reached only when withCheck gets headSnapshots === undefined; the only such caller is readNote(version) when readHeadRecord returns null (:2124-2130). Every other withCheck caller passes a Map (:762, :2139-2140, :2196, :2305-2306). The platform always writes the head and the version in one commit (src/core/work-graph/notes/note-service.ts:705-707, :829-835, :1504-1505) and the record store has no delete (PreparedCommit has no removal, src/core/record-store/ports.ts:110-125). A version without a head is therefore a hand-edited or damaged store, not a platform state; U stands.
rows.proposal_note: Deleting the fallback and answering unavailable 'the note head is missing' is safe: the fallback currently ends in checkNotes -> not_found (note-views.ts:1259 -> note-read-model.ts:483-489), so only the impossible orphan-version case changes code. checkNotes itself stays for core-routes.ts:666 and note-tool.ts:48.

rows.evidence: The arrow at :315 is reached only when readMessage returns not_found (src/core/work-graph/views/undelivered-reply-notices.ts:313-316). readUndeliveredReplies built the DTO from a record it decoded at its own lookup key (src/core/work-graph/communication/mailbox-service.ts:3272-3288), and readMessage loads that same key (mailbox-service.ts:1435-1453). The store has no delete (src/core/record-store/ports.ts:110-125) and the lookup index and snapshot are committed atomically, so a missing record between the two reads means a hand-edited or foreign store, not a platform writer; U stands.
rows.proposal_note: Codex's keep-untested and Claude's delete :314-316 are both safe: line :317 still returns the non-ready read, and stableDamage remains used at :321, :325, :338 and :341. Delete only if the lead prefers not_found to propagate; do not add a tamper test.

rows.evidence: compareText is called only in the sort tie-break when compareNoticePositions(left.position, right.position) === 0 (src/core/work-graph/views/undelivered-reply-notices.ts:294-296), and compareNoticePositions already compares itemKey after the cursor sequence (src/core/work-graph/views/notice-position.ts:42-49). Each position's itemKey is the item's own key (:350), and the seen map refuses or skips duplicates before push (:252, :272-281), so two distinct items can never have equal positions and sort never compares an element with itself. The local tie-break is therefore dead; D2 stands.
rows.proposal_note: Deleting compareText (:486-488) and using compareNoticePositions directly is safe. The same dead tie-break pattern is at automatic-rework-notices.ts:265 and note-review-notices.ts:141 (outside this batch), which the lead may want to treat together.
